content: Pseudoephedrine and triprolidine are prescribed to alleviate symptoms such as itchy and watery eyes, sneezing, and a runny or congested nose caused by hay fever, allergies, or the common cold. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. This medication is available in capsules, tablets, extended-release capsules, and liquid form for oral administration. It is typically taken every 4 to 6 hours or every 12 hours (for extended-release capsules) as needed. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take pseudoephedrine and triprolidine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed. Swallow extended-release capsules whole; do not open them. Do not administer this medication to children under 12 years of age unless directed by a doctor. Before taking pseudoephedrine and triprolidine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to pseudoephedrine, triprolidine, or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially those for asthma, high blood pressure, or seizures; muscle relaxants; narcotics (pain medications); sedatives; sleeping pills; tranquilizers; and vitamins. Do not take this medication if you have used an MAO inhibitor in the past two weeks. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had heart disease, high blood pressure, difficulty urinating (due to an enlarged prostate gland), glaucoma, asthma, an overactive thyroid gland, ulcers, seizures, or diabetes. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking pseudoephedrine and triprolidine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate the drowsiness caused by this medication. Pseudoephedrine and triprolidine may cause an upset stomach. To minimize this, take the medication with food or milk. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. This medication may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: dry mouth, nose, and throat; upset stomach; difficulty sleeping; chest congestion; headache; diarrhea; or drowsiness. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: muscle weakness, vision problems, skin rash, excitement, difficulty breathing, fast heartbeat, tremors, difficulty or painful urination, or hallucinations. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature and away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist about the appropriate disposal method. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the victim has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have any questions about refilling your prescription.
